claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified on the strength of aggregate performance only if the small-business support slice weakness is expressly disclosed, because no approved mitigation currently removes exposure and small-sample uncertainty does not make the certification clean.
specific_concerns: The available admissible record is only the actor's summary, not the underlying contents of the cited evidence.
The exact numeric claims about aggregate performance and slice underperformance are not independently verifiable from the admissible evidence provided to the auditor.
The packet asserts disclosure is required, but the underlying basis for treating the slice issue as a material weakness is not directly shown in the admissible record.
The recommended action is only supportable if the certification actually includes the stated disclosure; that final linkage is not evidenced here.
unsupported_claims: The model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by 2.2 percentage points.
The small-business support slice is 1.1 points below its warning threshold and 2.6 points below its preferred threshold.
No approved mitigation currently removes exposure because the only mitigation is still a draft.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BMCARD-015-A through BMCARD-015-E, not just their IDs.
Provide the evaluation results showing the aggregate score, the small-business support slice score, and the applicable thresholds.
Provide the policy or rubric used to determine that the subgroup weakness is material and therefore disclosure-triggering.
Provide the mitigation artifact and approval status showing whether any mitigation is approved and whether it removes deployment exposure.
Provide the actual proposed certification language to confirm the disclosure is included in the certification record.
decision_criteria: Certification may proceed only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness, but they do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty may reduce confidence but does not convert an unresolved materiality question into a clean certification.
A compliant determination requires admissible evidence sufficient to support the actor's factual predicates, not just the actor's characterization of them.
